- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates when true values are trending downward from a recent peak — especially in the 10–20 day window.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the 20–30 day forecast window, suggesting it underweights recent downward momentum.
- Model often fails to adjust for “lagged” historical patterns — e.g., if history shows a 30-day downtrend, model still forecasts upward.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility — forecasts spike higher after minor price drops, then collapse, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Model underestimates when true values are near or below 70 — especially in the 15–25 day window — suggesting it underweights low-price regimes.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — forecasts are anchored to recent high values (e.g., 80–85) and fail to adjust for subsequent corrections.
